**About The Team**
The Storage teams build and operate online stateful systems and abstractions that are reliable, efficient, secure and easy to use for DoorDash Engineering. The teams are responsible for understanding Product Engineering’s evolving needs and developing platform and infrastructure capabilities to serve them. The team currently supports CockroachDB, Cassandra, Kafka and Redis as well as data abstraction services to reduce the complexity of interacting with storage systems for Product Engineers.
  
  
**About The Role**
The Storage team is building and operating a high-performance, scalable, and reliable data abstraction layer that optimizes both efficiency and reliability. Our goal is to create a platform that manages itself and fades into the background—empowering engineers to focus on delivering product experiences our customers love.
  
  
This role is available across two teams within Storage, each solving unique and high-impact challenges:
  
  

* One team owns DoorDash’s vector storage infrastructure—operating and evolving vector search systems and future storage indexing systems. You’ll tackle challenges in distributed systems, performance, and reliability, turning complex, stateful indexing workloads into scalable, developer-friendly services used across the company.
* One team builds and operates the distributed data platform powering DoorDash's largest stateful workloads -- including Cassandra, which backs critical product surfaces across DoorDash, Wolt, and Roo. You'll design high-throughput data abstractions, smart clients, and platform services that make distributed data reliable and easy to work with at multi-petabyte, multi-million-QPS scale, with opportunities to go deep on distributed systems internals and contribute to the open-source Cassandra ecosystem.

If you're passionate about distributed systems, developer experience, and building foundational infrastructure at scale, we'd love to hear from you.
  
  
You must be located in San Francisco, Sunnyvale, Seattle, or the New York Metro Area for this hybrid position. You will report into the Engineering Manager on our Storage team within the Core Infrastructure Organization.
  
  
**You’re Excited About This Opportunity Because You Will…**

* Build and optimize distributed storage systems that improve data reliability, consistency, and performance.
* Own high-leverage control-plane services with clear customer impact, strong reliability requirements, and room for deep technical exploration.
* Develop and maintain data abstraction services tailored for high-throughput, low-latency workloads.
* Implement and refine caching strategies using Redis, Memcached, and similar technologies to enhance system efficiency.
* Collaborate with teams across infrastructure, platform, and application layers to ensure seamless data access and storage performance.
* Drive innovation in storage architecture by identifying and addressing scalability and efficiency challenges in distributed systems.

**We’re Excited About You Because…**

* You have 2+ years of fulltime working experience in designing, building and maintaining scalable, distributed data infrastructure.
* You are proficient in GoLang, or Java with a deeper expertise in multi-threading, distributed systems and databases.
* You have deep expertise in NoSQL databases (Cassandra, DynamoDB, or similar) and distributed caching systems (Redis, Memcached).
* You have built and optimized high-scale data storage systems with a focus on reliability, availability, and performance.
* You have expertise in workflow/orchestration engines (Temporal/Cadence/Argo, job runners) and modeling long-running, stateful workflows.
* You thrive in a fast-paced, execution-driven environment and have a proven track record of delivering impactful storage solutions.

Job Description

Purified tap water, food and beverage production, massive data centers, and advanced manufacturing facilities all depend on industrial software that can't go down. As a Software Solutions Engineer I, you'll be the person customers call when something breaks, working through root causes with them in real time. 



This role is part of Inductive Automation's national expansion into our brand-new Columbia, Maryland office. You'll work alongside the engineers who built our Software Support Services division into the best in the business, and you'll collaborate directly with colleagues at our headquarters in Folsom, California. You'll also get to know industrial automation from the front row, working with end users and system integrators who are building the future of industrial tech. This is a full-time role with on-site work required Monday-Friday from 6:00 AM - 3:00 PM.  



Whether your background is in Computer Science or Electrical Engineering/Controls, you’ll help bridge Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT). 



You’ll like this job if: 

You love connecting the dots between a timestamp, a cryptic error message, and a weird software behavior. You see a complex failure as a puzzle, and you won't walk away until you find the root cause. You're also patient and warm with people, even when they're stressed.  You like working as part of a team with both colleagues and customers, in an environment where everyone steps up to help where needed. 



Responsibilities

 - Solving hard problems. Owning complex technical cases: writing and debugging different coding languages, tracking down root-cause architectural issues across platforms, and navigating issues spanning multiple layers and different technologies. 

 - Working directly with customers. Helping customers and system integrators by phone and email, whether they're technical or not, and keeping them informed while you work. 

 - Getting very good at root-cause analysis. Building diagnostic skills that will serve you for your whole career. 

 - Documenting as you go. Keeping clear records of ticket progress, issue breakdowns, and resolutions. They become the knowledgebase articles of tomorrow.

 - Leaving your fingerprints on Ignition. Proposing enhancements, advocating for fixes, and partnering with Software Engineering to shape future releases. The more you master Ignition, the more your ideas drive the roadmap. 

 - Growing with the work. Level I is the start of a path through the Senior Software Solutions Engineer role, where you'll take on the toughest cases and help train the next engineers in.

 - Getting Ignition Certified. Completing Core and Gold Ignition certifications funded by Inductive Automation before touching a live customer system. 

 - Be part of a global team.  Collaborating with colleagues at our Folsom, California headquarters and Australia branch. 



Requirements

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Mechatronics, or equivalent hands-on experience with SCADA systems, PLCs, or industrial control networks is required 

 - Comfort writing code (Java, Python, etc.) and SQL queries 

 - Familiarity with relational databases (MS SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle, etc.) and how tables relate 

 - Experience with Windows, Linux, and macOS; command line skills are a plus 

 - Comfort troubleshooting live alongside customers 

 - Confidence learning unfamiliar subjects on the fly 

 - Strong written and verbal communication, and the ability to listen, acknowledge frustration, and steer a tense situation toward a solution 

 - Must be able to work on-site, Monday - Friday from 6:00 AM - 3:00 PM 

Not required, but preferred:  

 - Customer Service experience 

 - Experience with PLCs (Rockwell/Allen-Bradley, Omron, Siemens, etc.), HMIs, or industrial networks 

 - Experience with Ignition or other SCADA/HMI platforms
